findings.statement: CXCR2 (rank 1) is almost entirely a neutrophil transcript in inflamed mucosa in Gubatan 2026 [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965], while Smillie (no neutrophils) assigns it to T/NK cells and Garrido-Trigo to myeloid, so the attribution does not replicate across datasets. After adjusting for cell composition the change shrinks to a small residual and the verdict is partly_composition [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409]. It is mainly a marker of neutrophil influx; any drug effect would be on recruited neutrophils, not on resident tissue.

CXCR1 (rank 2) is a neutrophil receptor, with nearly all its inflamed-mucosa transcripts coming from neutrophils [gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962]. Its bulk rise should be read as neutrophil arrival. Composition adjustment was not run for it.

CXCL8 is made by myeloid cells in Smillie (macrophages) and the lineage replicates in the second dataset, but in inflamed mucosa most of its transcripts come from neutrophils [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]. After composition adjustment the change is no longer significant and the verdict is composition [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0527]. It behaves as a marker of myeloid and neutrophil influx; adjustment may over-correct, so this is not proof of pure influx.

MMP1 comes mainly from stromal cells, above all inflammatory fibroblasts, and the attribution replicates in the second dataset [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871]. The change stays significant after composition adjustment, although the verdict is partly_composition [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]. This is a stromal tissue-level change and not neutrophil influx, which supports a fibroblast target.

DUOX2 is an epithelial gene (enterocytes) and the attribution replicates in the second dataset [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]. It keeps a significant change after composition adjustment [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]. This is evidence of epithelial activation inside the tissue, not of cell influx.

CHI3L1 is stromal (inflammatory fibroblasts), replicated in the second dataset [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.941], although neutrophils also contribute a sizeable fraction in Gubatan. It keeps a significant change after adjustment [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]. It is mostly an intrinsic fibroblast activation marker.

IDO1 is expressed by myeloid cells (macrophages, DC1) and the lineage replicates, with a low neutrophil contribution [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.072]. It keeps a significant change after adjustment (partly_composition) [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]. This points to activation of resident myeloid cells and enterocytes, so it is a possible cell-type target.

OSMR is stromal (inflammatory fibroblasts and WNT2B+ fibroblasts), replicated in the second dataset. The unadjusted change is [gene=OSMR; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; unadjusted_log2fc=1.1368] and the adjusted change is much smaller but still significant [gene=OSMR; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.2528]. Most of the bulk rise tracks composition, with a residual fibroblast-intrinsic component; the adjustment may over-correct.

CD274 (PD-L1) is mainly neutrophil-derived in inflamed mucosa [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687], with a diffuse non-neutrophil origin in Smillie (plasma, macrophages, enterocytes). It retains a significant change after adjustment [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]. Its cell of origin is mixed, so it is not a clean cell-specific target.

S100A8 is a myeloid gene in Smillie and Garrido-Trigo, and in inflamed mucosa nearly all of it comes from neutrophils [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]. A residual change survives adjustment [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231]. It is a marker of neutrophil and myeloid infiltration, with some activation component.

AQP9 transcripts in inflamed mucosa are almost all neutrophil-derived [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92], so its high convergence rank mostly reflects neutrophil influx. Composition adjustment was not run.

SLC26A2 falls in UC, is expressed by epithelial cells (immature enterocytes, replicated), and its decrease is the only one among those tested with an intrinsic verdict, remaining after adjustment [gene=SLC26A2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-1.4638]. This is a true loss of epithelial function, not dilution by influx, but it is a loss of function and not a drug-target candidate.

caveats: Lineage scores also rise when resident cells become activated, so composition adjustment can over-correct; partly_composition and composition verdicts are not proof of pure influx.
Smillie 2019 captured no neutrophils, so neutrophil-derived genes (CXCR2, CXCL8, S100A8) are attributed to other cells there; Gubatan 2026 is the reference for neutrophil share.
Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance; dissociation protocols enrich some fractions.
Composition adjustment was run only for a subset of candidates; CXCR1, AQP9 and others rest on cell-type attribution alone.
Many neutrophil-derived genes (CXCR2, CXCL8) may still be valid targets in recruited neutrophils; the data decide only whether the signal is tissue-intrinsic.
